- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) and prices are falling, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to reverse; adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate in early periods when sentiment is volatile; increase forecast by 1–3% for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 1.0, 0.3, 1.0), model overfits short-term momentum; dampen forecast by 0.5–1.5% for each alternating cycle.
